newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria postpones ruling on Balkanbank insolvency.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria postpones ruling on Balkanbank insolvency.

text.p: A Bulgarian court on Thursday postponed ruling on an insolvency suit against state-owned Balkanbank for two months pending completion of an experts' report on the bank's financial state, a court official said.
"The Sofia City Court postponed ruling until May 5 because the experts have not completed their statement on the bank's assets-to-liabilities ratio," the official told reporters.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) put Balkanbank in receivership on September 23 and filed an insolvency suit against it on October 31.

The court ruling was first postponed on December 9 to give time to experts appointed by the court to prepare an independent report on the bank's assets-to-liabilities ratio at the time when the insolvency suit was filed.
The BNB last year opened bankruptcy procedures against 15 state and private banks or a third of Bulgaria's banks.
Only one of them, Madan-based private Crystalbank, has been declared insolvent by the court so far.
Court rulings are expected on state-owned Mineralbank, Private Agricultural and Investment Bank and private Trade and Savings Bank by end-March.
